name: Main idea / primary purpose
description: The passage's central claim, or why the author wrote it. Traps: too narrow (one paragraph's point), too broad, right topic with the wrong verb ("refute" vs "qualify").

name: Detail (stated information)
description: What the passage says explicitly. Traps: right words from the wrong part of the passage, distortions of degree or scope.

name: Inference (supported, unstated)
description: What must be true or is most strongly supported, including what a scholar or group the passage cites believes or would agree with. Traps: plausible but unsupported, true in the world but not in the passage, extreme wording, the author's view given for a cited party's.

name: Function / purpose of a part
description: Why a sentence, example or paragraph is there (to concede, illustrate, qualify, contrast). Traps: an accurate paraphrase that misstates its role.

name: Author's attitude / tone
description: The author's stance and degree of certainty toward a view or person. Traps: tone too strong ("scathing") or the opposite polarity; a view the author only reports, or floats as speculation, read as one the author holds.

name: Structure / organization
description: How the passage or a paragraph is built (claim then counterexample, two views then a synthesis). Traps: one move out of order or missing.

name: Word or phrase in context
description: What a word or phrase means as used here. Traps: the word's common sense where the passage uses a secondary one.

name: Application / analogy
description: Which new situation parallels, would be explained by, or would be judged by the passage's idea.

name: Select-all / EXCEPT verification
description: Each statement checked independently against the text (select-all or EXCEPT). Traps: a true-in-the-world but unsupported choice; one half-right choice.

name: Argument: weaken
description: New information that most undermines the conclusion, usually by attacking an assumption. Traps: out-of-scope facts, attacks on a premise rather than the link.

name: Argument: strengthen / support
description: New information that most supports the conclusion or a proposed explanation. Traps: supports a related but different conclusion.

name: Argument: assumption
description: The unstated premise the argument depends on (negation test). Traps: sufficient but not necessary assumptions, too-strong wording.

name: Argument: resolve a paradox
description: Information that explains how two apparently conflicting facts can both be true; the hard form adds a constraint (explain the discrepancy while leaving a stated theory intact). Traps: explains only one side, or resolves it by breaking the constraint.

name: Argument: evaluate
description: The question whose answer would most help judge the argument (one answer strengthens, the other weakens).

name: Argument: flaw / method
description: The reasoning error or technique (sampling, causation from correlation, equivocation).

name: Argument: role of a statement (boldface)
description: What part a highlighted statement plays: conclusion, premise, counter-premise, intermediate conclusion.

name: Argument: conclusion / inference
description: What the statements most strongly support, the point the passage emphasizes, or which statement the information directly contradicts. Traps: a claim one notch too strong, or one the passage merely does not mention.

name: Argument: complete the passage
description: Which statement most logically fills the blank that ends the passage, often after "since" or "because", so the key is the missing premise that makes the conclusion follow. Traps: a choice that restates the conclusion, or supports a neighbouring claim.
